title: Form Integration
description: Integrate React Query with form libraries like React Hook Form for seamless server-state management.

data.text: Forms are one of the most common places where server state and client state collide. React Query excels at managing the server-side aspects of formsâ€”fetching initial data, submitting mutations, and updating the cacheâ€”while libraries like React Hook Form handle the client-side form state and validation.

data.title: Core Principle
data.text: React Query manages server state (data from APIs). React Hook Form manages client state (form inputs, validation, touched fields). Let each library do what it does best.

data.title: React Query Responsibilities
items: Fetching initial form data from the server
Updating the cache after successful submission
Managing loading and error states for data operations

data.caption: Data flow between React Query and React Hook Form
data.definition:
graph TB
    A[API] -->|fetch| B[React Query Cache]
    B -->|query data| C[React Hook Form defaultValues]
    C -->|user input| D[Form State]
    D -->|onSubmit| E[Mutation]
    E -->|success| F[Invalidate + Reset]
    F -->|updated data| B
    style B fill:#4f46e5
    style E fill:#059669

data.text: The first step in form integration is loading existing data. Use `useQuery` to fetch the record, then pass the data to React Hook Form's `reset` function. This keeps the form state in sync with the server without manual state management.

data.title: useQuery + React Hook Form
data.content: Use useQuery to fetch data and populate React Hook Form default values

data.title: Async Default Values
data.text: React Hook Form supports async default values via a function. This pairs perfectly with React Query because the query may not have resolved yet when the form mounts.
When the user submits the form, use `useMutation` to send the data to the server. On success, update the React Query cache so any other components displaying this user data also update automatically.

data.title: Form Submission Mutation
data.content: Handle form submission with useMutation and update the cache

data.text: Optimistic updates make forms feel instant by updating the cache before the API call completes. If the call fails, roll back to the previous state. This pattern is especially effective for small, frequent updates like toggling a setting.

data.title: Optimistic Form Updates
data.content: Use optimistic updates to make forms feel instant with rollback on failure

data.title: Server-Side Validation Errors
data.content: Map API validation errors back to React Hook Form errors object

items.text: Query data populates form default values
Server validation errors map to form errors

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: React Query fetches data; React Hook Form manages input state
Use reset() to sync server data into form fields
useMutation handles form submission and cache updates
Optimistic updates make forms feel instant
Map server validation errors to form error state
data.takeaway: Forms are where server state meets client state. React Query handles the server side, while React Hook Form handles the client side.
